segments: Background: Historical baggage has left Nix with two command-line interfaces: nix-xxx, the older standalone commands, and nix xxx, the newer unified subcommands. Enabling nix-command and flakes makes the new CLI available, but the old commands are still used for older profiles, channels, and specific administrative operations. Parts of the new CLI remain experimental; consult the help for your installed version.
1. The everyday survival kit: just remember these 4
For everyday use, start by understanding these four types of operation and their effects:
Scenario
Command
Explanation
Apply configuration changes
Run after editing configuration.nix or flake.nix. With Flakes, this is usually sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake .#主机名
Update all system software
For a channels-based configuration, update the channel, then build and activate; for a Flake workflow, update the lock first.
Undo a broken system change
Roll back immediately to the previous generation. A reboot is not required, but is recommended to verify the result.
Clean up when the disk is full
Delete all old generations and reclaim space in /nix/store. Afterward, you cannot roll back to the deleted generations.
2. Old and new CLI counterparts

After enabling experimental-features = [ "nix-command" "flakes" ], the new subcommands provide corresponding functionality. Profile formats and dependency sources differ, however, so the commands in this table are not unconditional drop-in replacements.
Old CLI
New CLI
Purpose
Install user-level software
Remove user-level software
View generation history
Build a derivation
Enter a temporary dependency environment
Update a channel or a Flake's locked inputs, respectively (these are different data sources)
Evaluate a Nix expression

** Note the exceptions**: nixos-rebuild (system management) and nix-collect-garbage (garbage collection) handle system rebuilding and profile-history cleanup combined with GC. nix-collect-garbage also works on non-NixOS systems, while nix store gc handles only unreferenced store objects.
3. Common new commands for development and testing

Run a program temporarily, without installing it:
nix run nixpkgs#cowsay -- "Hello NixOS"

Enter a temporary shell environment:
nix shell nixpkgs#python3 nixpkgs#postgresql

Enter the project's development environment (requires a flake.nix in the project root with devShells configured):
nix develop
4. Advanced generation management

A generation is like a game's "save point." switch/boot operations that update the system profile can record a new save point; build/dry-build alone do not. Old generations are not deleted automatically.
Operation
Command
List all system generations
Switch to a specific generation (for example, number 50)
sudo nix-env --profile /nix/var/nix/profiles/system --switch-generation 50, then run that profile's bin/switch-to-configuration switch to activate it
Delete a specific generation
Keep only the latest 5 generations
Keep generations from the past 30 days
sudo nix-collect-garbage --delete-older-than 30d (recommended; safer than -d)
Roll back through GRUB at boot
After rebooting, select "NixOS - All configurations" in the GRUB menu
Store GC and deleting profile history

The new nix CLI includes nix store gc to clean the underlying store directory, but it does not automatically delete old generations for you. If you use only nix store gc, the old generations remain, so their packages are not considered "unreferenced" and cannot be removed.
nix-collect-garbage collects only unreachable objects by default. Adding -d or --delete-older-than first deletes old history from the profiles it finds. Running it as root may affect multiple users' profiles; you must understand the scope of its scan.
History interfaces for the system profile
The new nix profile provides interfaces for the new profile workflow. When handling NixOS system-level configurations at /nix/var/nix/profiles/system, the old and new commands differ as follows:

If you want to clean up with the new commands, this is an alternative:
You can use nix profile wipe-history in place of nix-env.

Why keep the traditional history interfaces and GC tools:
Retaining generations by age or by count is a maintenance-policy choice. nix-collect-garbage --delete-older-than 30d combines "delete generations" and "reclaim space" in one operation. With the new commands, these are two separate steps: first delete generations with nix profile wipe-history, then reclaim space with nix store gc. This makes it easier to control history-deletion scope and space reclamation separately.
5. Declarative automatic maintenance: put it in your configuration
To avoid running cleanup commands manually, enable automatic maintenance directly in configuration.nix:
6. Remember commands by responsibility
Everyday system management: nixos-rebuild. Temporary programs and development environments: nix run, nix shell, and nix develop.
Profile, channel, and older-expression maintenance: nix-env, nix-build, nix-shell, and nix-channel still have uses, depending on your workflow.
Installation and recovery: nixos-install, nixos-enter, and nixos-generate-config may still be useful for recovery after installation.

Configuration files are a good fit for stable system and user environments; imperative environments are useful for temporary exploration. Garbage collection does not automatically remove all installed software, nor does it preserve rollback points that have already been removed.

The command table uses the current Nix 2.34 interface. nix profile install is a compatibility alias for add; older versions may have only the old name. A package output being in the store does not mean it is permanently installed. Outputs may remain in the store after a temporary environment ends and later be reclaimed by GC.
